items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then we had another quartet with a saxophone player and a drummer named Tony Brazinski.

ctx.x: So this the late 50's; this is already after Brown v. Board of Education?

Yeah mid 50's, I think. So yeah, you might have some dates there that might be more accurate than my memory serves me. So, I took foundry in the early years as a vocation but they had band there so I took band as well. I played acoustic bass the first year in the concert band and then a group of guys… …a guy names James Willis, who played clarinet but also play bass and all this time Ahmad's at The Pershing. “But Not For Me” was popular then. He was now was on Argo or Chess Records then. There was another guy who…
So you were a dance band?
